steps_walked.title: Row U: the finished translations in 12 languages, the Patterns-lens gate panel, the encrypted unlock path, newsletter filing with its announcement and undo, sparse commodity price bars, and the religious calendars left in place
prerequisites: A checkout of main at or after 462145c with its .venv installed. That build includes PR #1137 (diagnostics package split), #1139 (FUTURE_DEVELOPMENTS reality check), #1140 (encrypted click-through variant), #1141 (newsletter attach and undo), and #1160 and #1161 (translations, Patterns gate, sparse overlay bars). Run every command from the app folder, the one that contains .venv.

Two new, empty THROWAWAY folders OUTSIDE any real data folder, for example ~/oo-rowU-empty (U1) and ~/oo-rowU-seeded (U2, U3, U5, U6, U7, U9). On Windows PowerShell set the variables like this: $env:OO_DATA_DIR="$HOME\oo-rowU-empty"; $env:OO_PORT="8011"; .venv\Scripts\open-omniscience.
The seeder in U2 writes straight into the database file. Run it only while NO app is running against ~/oo-rowU-seeded. After U2, keep that app (port 8010) running through U9.
Airplane mode ON throughout: the plane icon in the top bar stays FILLED. Every throwaway boot starts offline, and nothing in row U needs the network.

For U7: 3 to 6 newsletter .eml files, each with a short text or HTML body. Real ones from a mail client work. For a delegated run, the session can write three minimal synthetic files into a scratch folder outside the repo instead: (1) From: newsletters@email.bbc.com, which should be filed under a publisher already tracked, since the catalogue is registered after the first unlock; (2) From: news@some-unknown-press.org, which should create a new, disabled source; (3) From: hello@substack.com with no List-Id, a bare platform address that the ladder should refuse and leave in the import bucket.
For a delegated (agent) run: Chromium plus Playwright. This sandbox has /opt/pw-browsers/chromium, as used by docs/audit/i18n-remainder-clickthrough-2026-09-18/walk.py.

U4 and U8 are OPTIONAL and need the maintainer's own machine: their real encrypted install, updated to the same main, and its passphrase. A cloud-sandbox session cannot reach them. Before U8, make a fresh backup of the real install (Settings → Data & backup → 'Export / Back up…').
Cleanup: stop each throwaway app with Ctrl+C, then delete ~/oo-rowU-empty and ~/oo-rowU-seeded. Everything U1 to U7 and U9 created lives inside them.

The row still does not fully close. On a fresh first launch the 'Where should your corpus live?' screen never appears, because /api/system/data-location answers 503 while locked (P2). The Calendar directory shows no religion or astronomy families, so U9 fails. At 375 px the Help page scrolls sideways, and several small translation and hover gaps remain (P3). U4 and U8 need the maintainer's own machine, and whether a delegated walk counts under Q1128 = a is still a ruling to record.

verdicts.title: The first-launch 'Where should your corpus live?' screen never appears, because the lock gate blocks its endpoint
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on my own fresh instance (port 8853, empty OO_DATA_DIR, booted with the console script, no passphrase variable). Path: language → legal → tick → 'Accept and continue'. The only /api/system/data-location response was 503 {"detail":"the database is locked: unlock it first","locked":true}. #view-datadir stayed hidden and #view-create showed. Control, same page and same flow: I fulfilled only that one request with the JSON the handler itself returns for this state. That JSON came from calling src.api.unlock.data_location() with OO_DATA_DIR pointed at a fresh folder: offerable:true, state:fresh. With it, 'Where should your corpus live? … Use the app's own data folder [selected] … Choose another folder … Continue' renders. So the lock middleware is the only thing blocking the step. The step is maintainer-asked (src/safety/data_location.py docstring, THE ASK 2026-07-14). No other path reaches it: a plaintext store never has a 'fresh' state. The default folder still works, so nothing is lost; the feature is simply dead on every install, silently. P2 stands. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/U-recheck/fresh.json, shots/U-D1-after-accept-real-en.png, shots/U-D1-control-200-datadir-en.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/api/unlock.py:75-93: ALLOWED_WHILE_LOCKED does not list /api/system/data-location. unlock.py:70-71: app_is_locked() is True for 'fresh'. src/api/main.py:751-763: the _lock_gate middleware answers 503 for every other path. src/static/unlock.html:340-345: legalToDataLocation() parses the 503 body, where info.offerable is undefined, and silently calls legalToPassphrase(). tests/test_data_location.py:283-292 mounts the router on a bare FastAPI() without the middleware, so no test can see this.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Add "/api/system/data-location" to ALLOWED_WHILE_LOCKED. The prefix match covers GET, POST /check and POST, and both POSTs already refuse with 409 unless the state is 'fresh', so nothing opens after a store exists. Add a test through the real src.api.main app, which runs the middleware, at state 'fresh', asserting 200 and offerable:true. Optionally make unlock.html treat a non-2xx answer as an error rather than as 'not offerable'. Also decide on unlock.html:336-339: its comment says an explicit OO_DATA_DIR skips the step, but the handler's offerable ignores explicit_override, and the existing test pins offerable to 'fresh' only.

verdicts.title: Calendar directory: the religion and astronomy families are hidden (the U9 'directory part FAIL')
verdicts.reason: The families are hidden by a deliberate filter shipped 2026-07-10, long before Q1135/RC13, not by anything in row U. shipped.csv row 2026-07-10 'B7: robots-dead default calendar feeds filtered from the loaded directory (honest single-provider set)'. The src/events/feeds.py:45-57 comment reads: 'calendar.google.com's robots.txt DISALLOWS its /calendar/ical/ paths … www.webcal.guru likewise disallows its download endpoints; cantonbecker.com + space.floern.com are robots-undetermined (fail-closed refuses them; the local Meeus astronomy already covers moons/eclipses). These are now filtered OUT of the loaded directory entirely … The bundled YAML keeps the full dated record'. Every one of the 8 religion families and the astronomy family sits only on those hosts, so none of them could ever produce an event. The gate does not ask for them to be shown. RC13 → (b) (RELEASE_0.4_GATE.md row U, and the 2026-09-18 amendment) sends the religious dates to a SEPARATE networked research session that is 'BRIEFED HERE AND NOT BUILT'. The same entry's 'nothing was removed from the agenda meanwhile' is true: the removal predates it. Re-measured: load_families() gives 241 families, kinds holidays 239 / civic 1 / community 1. The YAML carries religion 8, science 1 and space 1. The walker's expectation 'Kind = religion lists 8 families' was a misread. The stale hint that advertises these families is a real defect, reported separately below.
verdicts.root_cause: Intended: src/events/feeds.py:58-60 (_DEAD_DEFAULT_HOSTS), :90-102 (feed filter and empty-family drop), per the 2026-07-10 B7 ruling.
verdicts.suggested_fix: None for the filtering. The religious dates belong to the RC13 = (b) networked session already briefed in the gate's §3 amendment log.

verdicts.title: Calendar directory hint advertises ~500 multi-provider feeds including religions, elections, space and astronomy that the directory does not serve
verdicts.reason: This is the half of the walker's U9 defect that survives. Measured on my encrypted seeded instance (8852), in Settings → Advanced → Calendar directory. The hint reads: 'A bundled directory of ~500 public calendar feeds (country holidays, religions, elections, UN days, space, astronomy)… When several providers publish the same calendar, they are grouped into one folder — you see the duplicate and can compare every source.' On the same screen the status reads '241 feeds · 241 folders', and the Kind select offers only all / civic / community / holidays. /api/events/feeds returns 241 families: holidays 239, civic 1 (UN days), community 1. Since B7 there is one provider per family, so the duplicate-folder sentence is false too. It is stale copy that describes features the reader cannot find, on the app's own honesty surface. Cosmetic in effect: P3. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/U-recheck/seeded_strip_price_moon_calendar.json (cal.*), shots/U-D2-calendar-hint-en.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/index.html:2724-2725: static hint text was not updated when the 2026-07-10 B7 load-time filter (src/events/feeds.py:58-102) cut the directory to 241 single-provider families.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Rewrite the hint to describe what load_families() actually serves: about 240 country-holiday feeds plus UN days and one community calendar, one provider each. Add one line saying that feeds whose hosts' robots.txt refuses them are withheld. Alternatively, render the counts from /api/events/feeds. Key the new strings ×12.

verdicts.title: The Help page scrolls sideways by 406 px at 375 px width
verdicts.reason: Reproduced by loading the app at 375x812 in en and pressing the top-bar '?'. Home measured scrollWidth - clientWidth = 0, Help measured 406. The widest element is a CODE inside a PRE (the User Manual's 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/…' install line), 815 px wide, with its right edge at 829. The .doc-layout grid is 301 px wide, but its single track resolves to 744.375px. The first <pre> is 744 px wide with scrollWidth 841. So the pre's own overflow-x:auto never engages: the grid track has already grown to the pre's min-content. Evidence: seeded_newsletter_narrow_help.json (help.*), shots/U-D3-help-375-en.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app.css:1622 (grid-template-columns:230px 1fr) and :1675 (grid-template-columns:1fr at ≤600px). A 1fr track has an 'auto' minimum, so it grows to the grid item's min-content, which includes the unbreakable <pre> line. The pre's overflow-x:auto (app.css:1648) does not lower the min-content contribution of its non-scrolling grid-item ancestor.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Use minmax(0,1fr) in both rules (230px minmax(0,1fr) at desktop, minmax(0,1fr) at ≤600px), or add .doc-layout > * { min-width:0 }. The existing .prose pre { overflow-x:auto } then scrolls inside the box.

verdicts.title: Home's at-a-glance strip stays in the previous language after a switch, and three of its counters are never translated
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on 8852 (encrypted, unlocked), switching with #lang-switch. In fr, 1 s and 5 s after the switch, the strip still read ARTICLES/SOURCES/KEYWORDS/COMMODITY PRICES… and 'Automatic collection: stopped · Your corpus stays on this machine…'. In ar right after the switch, the strip and status line were entirely English on an rtl page (shots/U-D4-strip-ar-after-switch.png). After the next live poll (within 45 s), fr showed MOTS-CLÉS, PRIX DES MATIÈRES PREMIÈRES and 'Collecte automatique: arrêté', but 'SOURCES QUALIFIED', 'SOURCES PENDING' and 'SOURCES CANDIDATES' stayed English, and the age note read 'à 09:31 PM (serveur occupé)' with an English 12-hour time (shots/U-D4-strip-fr-after-poll.png). /api/database/stats returns exactly those nine keys. fr.json has no 'sources qualified', 'sources pending' or 'sources candidates' key, and the i18n gates cannot see them because the string is built by k.replace(/_/g,' '). Not counted here: the '6,418' English grouping in fr is the recorded deliberate omission for bare toLocaleString() (60 sites, OPEN_QUEUE). Evidence: seeded_strip_price_moon_calendar.json (strip.*), extra.json.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-home.js:21-29: HOME_STAT_LABELS lacks sources_qualified/sources_pending/sources_candidates, and the fallback t(k.replace(/_/g,' ')) has no key in any locale. app-home.js:46: toLocaleTimeString([], …) uses the browser locale, not the UI language. index.html:247: the strip sits inside [data-i18n-dyn], so the i18n walker skips it (i18n.js:58). app-boot.js:41-135: the one oo:langchange listener repaints the strip's Wikipedia figure and failure line, but never calls renderHomeStats or renderHomeStatus. So the strip waits for refreshHomeLive (app-home.js:844).
verdicts.suggested_fix: Keep the last /api/database/stats payload and scheduler running flag. In the oo:langchange listener, call renderHomeStats(cached.counts, cached) and renderHomeStatus(cachedRunning), without a fetch. Add the three labels to HOME_STAT_LABELS and key them ×12. Pass the UI locale (uiLangCode()) to toLocaleTimeString.

verdicts.title: The newsletter caveat has no hover mark and does not open the shared hover bubble
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on 8852 by importing the walker's four .eml files through Settings → Data & backup. #nl-attach-caveat carries its title ('the ruled publisher ladder run at import time: a Public Suffix List eTLD+1 …'), but its className stays 'card-caveat', and hovering never shows #oo-tip. That holds on two hovers after a 3 s wait and again after a full page reload. The count <b> beside it, created through innerHTML, has class oo-tip-target and opens the bubble with 'How this was decided: new-email-source · etld1'. So invariant #17 ('a MutationObserver marks future surfaces, so the convention cannot be forgotten') has a gap: a title added to an element that already exists is never marked. The caveat itself is visible, so informed consent holds; only the layered method misses the app's bubble. A real browser would still show the native tooltip. P3. Evidence: seeded_newsletter_narrow_help.json (nl.caveat_hover*, nl.count_hover).
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-boot.js:268-275: ooTipInit marks [title] elements once at boot and afterwards only for childList addedNodes. It never observes attribute changes. src/static/app-settings.js:1424 sets .title on the static #nl-attach-caveat (index.html:1991, which has no title at load). The textContent write at :1423 adds only a text node, which the observer skips because of the nodeType===1 check.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Generic fix: observe attributes as well, with {childList:true, subtree:true, attributes:true, attributeFilter:['title']}, and mark m.target on attribute mutations. That closes the gap for every surface that sets .title later. The show()/hide() title swaps only re-add a class that is already there. Local fix: add classList.add('oo-tip-target') in loadNewsletterAttach.

verdicts.title: In the newsletter source rows the count runs into the name ('BBC News1', 'some-unknown-press.org disabled2')
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on 8852 after the import. The #nl-attach-body .vr rows have innerText 'some-unknown-press.org disabled2' and 'BBC News1'. Each row computes display:block, and the name span's right edge (x 493 / 348) equals the count <b>'s left edge, so nothing separates the two. 'disabled2' can read as one word. It is a readability problem, not a data one: P3. Evidence: seeded_newsletter_narrow_help.json (nl.rows_innerText, nl.row_layout), shots/U-D6-rows-en.png.
verdicts.root_cause:
src/static/app-settings.js:1413-1417 builds each row as
name…count
with no separator. The only .vr rules are scoped to .vitals-pop (src/static/app.css:835-839), so outside the task-manager popover the row is an unstyled block.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Add a scoped rule such as #nl-attach-body .vr { display:flex; justify-content:space-between; gap:10px; }, which mirrors the .vitals-pop .vr rule. Alternatively, put a ' · ' between the span and the <b>.

verdicts.title: Two first-run dialogs open on top of each other on a fresh install, in an unpredictable order
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on my fresh 8853 by completing language → legal → create passphrase, which lands at /?wikiwizard=1#home. Five seconds later both #wiki-wizard.open and #guide-wizard.open were true. A read-only showModal hook recorded the order ['wiki-wizard@2849', 'guide-wizard@3407']: the guide went on top, and elementFromPoint at the wizard's own centre hits guide-wizard. The walker saw the other order in one of two runs, which fits two independent async chains racing. Nothing is blocked (close the top one, then the other), so P3. Evidence: fresh.json (C.dialogs_after_entry), shots/U-D7-stacked-dialogs-en.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-boot.js:555-558 calls openWikiWizard() when ?wikiwizard=1 is present. That function is async: it awaits /api/wiki/languages and /api/scheduler/config, then calls showModal (src/static/app-sources.js:1323-1350). Independently, app-boot.js:213 calls checkEmptyCorpus(), which awaits /api/database/stats and then calls openGuide() (src/static/app-backup.js:2705-2709 → app-core.js:785-789 showModal). Neither checks whether the other is open or pending, so the order depends on which fetch resolves first.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Sequence the two. In checkEmptyCorpus, when ?wikiwizard=1 is present or #wiki-wizard is open, defer openGuide() to the wiki wizard's 'close' event (dlg.addEventListener('close', openGuide, {once:true})), so exactly one first-run dialog is open at a time and the order is deterministic.

verdicts.title: The Price chart's axis label and the Agenda moon hovers keep the previous language after a switch; the moon method sentence is English in every language
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on 8852. Dy Price subtab: the svg reads 'Price USD/kg' in en. After switching to fr, the tab label becomes 'Prix' but the svg still reads 'Price USD/kg'. Selecting another subtab and then Price again leaves it unchanged. Opening the window fresh in fr gives 'Prix USD/kg'. Agenda month view: the moon title is 'Last quarter moon 07:52 UTC — …' in en and is unchanged after the switch to fr. Leaving the tab and coming back gives 'Dernier quartier 07:52 UTC — Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms (2nd ed.) ch. 49: mean lunar phase + periodic and planetary corrections; computed locally, … typically within ~2 minutes; …', so the method and accuracy tail is English even on a fresh fr render. Newly found in the same class: the month grid's weekday headings stay 'Mon Tue … Sun' after the switch and only become 'lun. mar. …' after navigating away and back. All of these are the frozen-locale class and one untranslated server string on a hover: P3. Evidence: seeded_strip_price_moon_calendar.json (price.*, moon.*), extra.json (agenda.*), shots/U-D8-price-fr-after-switch.png, shots/U-D8-moon-fr.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-analysis.js:538 bakes t9('Price') into the overlay SVG when it is drawn. src/static/app-agenda.js:1252 (month) and :1311 (week) build the title and weekday names once, at render time. They concatenate the server's moon.method and moon.acc, English constants _METHOD/_ACCURACY in src/events/astronomy.py, without t(). None of these renderers is registered in the oo:langchange listener (src/static/app-boot.js:41-135). The i18n gates cannot see server-sent strings.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Register the agenda grid re-render and the price-overlay redraw in the one oo:langchange listener, redrawing from retained payloads with no fetch, as _anRepaintXLang and _renderPatternsGate already do. Pass moon.method, moon.acc, season.method and season.acc through t(). Key the few fixed Meeus method and accuracy strings ×12, the same way loadNewsletterAttach already does t(d.caveat).

verdicts.title: The Commodities chart is not redrawn when the window gets narrower
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on 8852. At 1440x950 on Commodities, the canvas style width is 900px and horizontal scroll is 0. After set_viewport_size(375x812) with no reload and a 2.5 s wait, horizontal scroll is 562, and the widest element is a CANVAS 900 px wide with its right edge at 937. As the walker found, loading the page directly at 375 px is fine. A real user narrowing a desktop window or rotating a tablet hits this. P3. Evidence: seeded_newsletter_narrow_help.json (narrow.*), shots/U-D9-commodities-narrowed-375.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-markets.js:1756-1775: ooChart measures el.clientWidth once and sizes the canvas in fixed px (W = min(avail, 900)). The only ResizeObserver (:1758-1766) handles the not-yet-laid-out zero-width case and disconnects after the first render, so nothing refits the chart when its host narrows.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Keep one ResizeObserver per chart host and re-run ooChart(el, seriesList, opts) when el.clientWidth differs from the drawn W by more than a few px, with a debounce and without refetching. Alternatively, give the canvas max-width:100% and map pointer events through getBoundingClientRect.
